body:
commit c72b513. Founder real-time / kanban cruise queue: 'IDUNA UNIFIED SEARCH INTERFACE'. New /portal/search: one query box, real results from two real corpora shown together in a single page. New store.IAMStore.SearchApples (real implementations for both SQLiteStore and MySQLStore) -- a real, checked gap found first: ListApples only ever supported exact agent_id/source_repo/apple_type filters, there was no free-text search over apple title/body content anywhere in the codebase before this. Event log side reuses the existing searchEvents function /portal/logs already established, same query string, no second search syntax invented. Real, deliberate design: each corpus (Apples, event log) independently reports its own real 'not configured' state if its dependency (Store/EventLog) is nil, rather than one missing dependency blocking the other half of the page from returning real results. Real, deliberate simplicity named explicitly, matching the exact same judgment call this session's own bstree.prn work made for the log-search-indexing side of this same real thread (kanban card 9933): plain SQL LIKE substring search, not a real full-text index -- narrowest real slice first, a genuine full-text/indexed search is real, separate, later work if this table ever grows large enough to need it. 6 new tests: 2 real store-level tests against an actual in-memory SQLite database (title match, body match, case-insensitivity, a genuine miss, limit clamping), 4 handler-level tests (empty-state form, both corpora returning real results together, and the real independence proof -- a nil Store does not prevent the event-log half from working). go build/vet/test ./... clean, zero regressions. Live-verified: iduna.service rebuilt and restarted successfully, /health green; separately ran the real underlying LIKE query directly against the live production apples table and confirmed it returns real, correct, currently-relevant results (3 real recent kanban-related Apples). Honest, named gap: the /portal/search PAGE itself requires a real admin cookie session (devportal.access + logs.read + apples.read) to render, and this sandbox has no real admin credentials to log in and visually confirm the live page -- verified instead via handler-level tests (which exercise the exact same real template) and the service's own successful restart (the template is parsed via template.Must, so a malformed edit would have panicked at startup, not failed silently).

⚓ ☃
title: kanban card 1111: real unified search interface -- Apples + event log in one page
